I've seen many data engineers assume that PySpark UDFs and Pandas UDFs are interchangeable, with similar performance characteristics. 
However, this couldn't be further from the truth. 

What most people do is use PySpark UDFs as a straightforward replacement for Pandas UDFs, without considering the underlying performance implications. 
They often use the `udf` function from PySpark SQL functions, like `udf(my_python_function, StringType())`, without realizing the overhead of serializing and deserializing data.

What actually works is using Pandas UDFs, which are optimized for performance and can take advantage of vectorized operations. 
By using `pandas_udf` from PySpark SQL functions, like `pandas_udf(my_python_function, StringType().toInt(), PandasUDFType.SCALAR)`, you can achieve significant performance gains. 
In my experience, Pandas UDFs can be up to 10x faster than PySpark UDFs for certain workloads.

When working with large datasets, every optimization counts, and using Pandas UDFs can be a game-changer. 
So, the next time you're working with PySpark, remember to use Pandas UDFs for performance-critical code paths.
